title: Mill Street tower approved; prohibited dog designation upheld
subtitle: Heritage permits, KPMG audit contract, Trussler Road deferral, 2025 calendar and regional speed camera concerns
overview: Council approved a zoning change for a 28-storey mixed-use building at 328-330 Mill Street {{vote:m1}}, citing the need for housing supply. It also deferred a rezoning at 60 Trussler Road to November 18 so the applicant and staff can discuss fewer and smaller units and a visual barrier {{vote:m12}}.

After an in-camera session on legal advice, Council ratified the Dog Designation Appeal Committee's prohibited designation of a dog, with modified conditions {{vote:m3}}. After the closed session, the Mayor reported that the dog must be turned over to the Humane Society or relocated outside Kitchener within 30 days. Council also awarded the city's audit contract to KPMG LLP {{vote:m10}}, approved heritage permits and a notice to designate a Courtland Avenue East property, and approved the 2025 meeting calendar {{vote:m16}}.

The Mayor updated Council on Waterloo Region's automated speed enforcement program. Councillors raised concerns about doubled fines under the administrative penalty system and about revenue sharing. Any change in Kitchener's position would need a motion at a special meeting the following week. The meeting also recognized long-serving volunteer groups and presented a record donation to the Food Bank of Waterloo Region.

decisions.detail: Council approved the zoning amendment for 328-330 Mill Street, with the by-law not taking effect until the Growing Together by-law is in force for those lands.
Council referred the rezoning to the November 18, 2024 meeting so the applicant and staff can discuss fewer and smaller units and options for a visual barrier.
Council ratified the appeal committee's prohibited dog designation, with modified conditions set out in report COR-2024-463.
Council awarded the audit services contract to KPMG LLP for three years, with options to renew for two more, for a total of $665,909 including HST.
Council approved a heritage permit to demolish the house and directed publication of a notice of intention to repeal the property's heritage designation by-law.
Council directed the Clerk to publish a notice of intention to designate the property as having cultural heritage value or interest.
Council approved the 2025 calendar and let the Mayor, with the CAO and Clerk, schedule extra planning committee meetings to meet legislated timelines.
Council approved the zoning by-law amendment for 9-27 Turner Avenue.

debate: On Mill Street, a councillor asked about the height increase from 20 to 28 storeys and about neighbours' concerns. Staff said the zoning already permits 28 storeys and that larger setbacks and separation reduce shadow and wind impacts. Staff said green standards and landscaping would be reviewed at site plan stage.

Councillors asked the applicant about amenities. A dog grooming room is typical in the applicant's buildings, outdoor dog and playground space was not yet programmed but could be considered, and some three-bedroom units are planned. One councillor welcomed the progress given the housing supply crisis.

On the dog appeal, the owner said the dog is a seizure and mental health support animal and that the owner had not found the hearing location. Staff said notice was sent by email and registered mail and that no evidence of service-animal status was before the committee. One councillor asked to refer it back, but no seconder was found.

Committee members said the dog had prior incidents and that conditions such as a muzzle had not been followed, so public safety justified the designation. One councillor opposed it out of sympathy for the owner's medical needs.

On speed cameras, councillors raised concerns about fines doubling under the administrative penalty system and about revenue sharing. Staff said a fair revenue-sharing agreement should be in place before the program expands.
